headline: A Urine Test Could Spare Women From Invasive Cancer Procedures
meta_description: Researchers at the University of Manchester developed a non-invasive test using urine and vaginal samples that could eliminate unnecessary internal procedures…
summary_short: A simple urine and vaginal fluid test correctly identified womb cancer in most cases while sparing 93% of healthy women from invasive procedures.
body:
Researchers at the University of Manchester have developed a non-invasive test that could transform how doctors screen for womb cancer. Using only urine and vaginal fluid samples—requiring no internal examination—the test correctly identified 80 of 99 womb cancer cases in a study of 1,864 women with postmenopausal bleeding across seven hospitals in north-west England. Perhaps most importantly, it returned a negative result for 93 percent of women who did not have the disease. The findings, published in The Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology, and Women's Health, offer hope to hundreds of thousands of women currently facing invasive diagnostic procedures.

Postmenopausal bleeding is alarming and demands urgent investigation: between five and 10 percent of women referred with this symptom do have womb cancer. But that means 90 to 95 percent don't. Today, those lower-risk women endure internal ultrasounds, biopsies, or hysteroscopy—procedures involving a camera inserted into the womb—only to receive a clean diagnosis. "Many women face invasive, uncomfortable tests that can be stressful as well as costly for health services," explained Prof. Emma Davidson of Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust. The new test would fast-track those truly at risk while giving reassurance to others far earlier.

The research team acknowledges the path ahead. The samples were assessed by highly trained specialist cytologists, and it remains unclear whether the same accuracy would be achieved in routine clinical settings. The test was also only studied in symptomatic women; its performance in asymptomatic women hasn't been established. But if further studies confirm these findings in practice, thousands of women annually could avoid unnecessary procedures—while those who do have cancer get answers faster.
quick_facts: Test uses urine and vaginal fluid only—no internal examination required
Correctly identified 80 of 99 womb cancers in Manchester study of 1,864 women
Returned negative result for 93% of women without the disease
Study conducted across seven hospitals in north-west England
